baseline.name: Kahn traversal with an adjacency matrix
baseline.approach: Store V-by-V edge flags and inspect a full row when releasing a course.

archived.name: Kahn traversal with adjacency lists and an edge pool
archived.space: O(V+E) adjacency/indegree storage plus a fixed 2000-element queue

why: Adjacency lists visit only actual outgoing edges, which matters when prerequisites are sparse.
quantitative_comparison: A matrix traversal can inspect V^2 neighbor slots. The archive processes V vertices and E adjacency nodes, storing V heads and E edges instead of V^2 flags. Pointer/node sizes differ, so no byte ratio is asserted; the asymptotic benefit is strongest when E is much smaller than V^2.
tradeoffs: The source has a fixed 2000-course queue, assumes valid IDs/rows, and leaks successful allocations on a partial-allocation failure. A matrix can be simpler for very small dense graphs.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
